name: Pomerol

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc and Malbec sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
There is no legal or agreed definition of old, so the words promise nothing on their own.
keyfacts: Pomerol is a Right Bank appellation in the Libournais, and its wine is predominately Merlot with Cabernet Franc in a supporting role.
Pomerol has no official classification, yet Château Pétrus is a worldwide byword for a great growth.
Gravel and sand terraces lie over Tertiary clay, and the subsoil holds iron oxides known locally as crasse de fer.
Pomerol's vineyard covers about 1,980 acres, and in 2009 its 140 mostly family estates averaged about 15 acres each.
Pomerol is for red wine only, and all its permitted grapes are red.
The wines must age until at least November 1 of the year after harvest and may go on sale from November 15.

notes: Pomerol is led by Merlot, with Cabernet Franc valued for the tannin and acidity it adds.
Its characteristic flavor is plum, sometimes tending to prune.
The wines are deeply colored and creamy, with supple tannins and lower acidity than other Bordeaux reds.
Clay soils give body and power, while lighter, sandier soils give less powerful wines that age less long.

blurb.text: A Right Bank appellation in Bordeaux, covering the commune of Pomerol and part of Libourne, whose wine is mostly Merlot with Cabernet Franc in support. It became AOC in 1936.
